html:
The Nicaraguan Revolution overthrew the Somoza dictatorship. On 19 July 1979 the guerrillas of the Sandinista National Liberation Front entered Managua after a national uprising.

The murder of the opposition newspaper editor Pedro Joaquín Chamorro in January 1978 set off strikes and revolts. The Sandinistas, named after Sandino, led risings in city after city, and the National Guard bombed its own towns. Some 30,000 or more died. The United States withdrew its support, and Somoza fled to Miami.

The new government, led by Daniel Ortega and others, nationalised the Somoza property, began land reform and the literacy campaign. Its ties to Cuba alarmed Washington, which armed the Contras. The revolution made Nicaragua a front of the Cold War.
sum: The Nicaraguan Revolution overthrew the Somoza dictatorship. On 19 July 1979 the guerrillas of the Sandinista National Liberation Front entered Managua after a national uprising.
